attempt: replace the log-P Gaussian smoothing in _build_wiggle with CAMB's calculate_psmooth recipe (divide by an Eisenstein & Hu no-wiggle spectrum, smooth that ratio, multiply back)
motivation: the residual was localised to the two-halo term (1-halo correct to 0.14% at k=4.17, two-halo low by 0.56% at k=0.5-2), and the dewiggle is the only shape-carrying factor there. _build_wiggle's own docstring admitted it smoothed log P directly and skipped the no-wiggle fit.
implemented: port of halofit.f90 Tk_nw_init / Tk_nw / Pk_nowiggle (equations 26 and 28-31 of astro-ph/9709112), normalised to the linear spectrum at knorm = 0.03, on CAMB's own wiggle grid (kmin 5e-3, kmax 5 h/Mpc, 512 uniform steps in log k), with CAMB's edge rule of leaving points within 3 sigma of either end unsmoothed
what_that_rules_out: it is not a sampling artefact: the dense CAMB grid gives 18.8% against 19.4% for a 48-point grid, so the difference is in the model, not the input spacing
diagnosis: the ratios come out ABOVE 1 (1.08, 1.15, 1.08, 1.04) where the previous version sat just below. _dewiggle computes d2_lin + (f-1)*d2_wiggle with f < 1, so it subtracts d2_wiggle; getting more power than CAMB means the new d2_wiggle is negative where CAMB's is positive, i.e. the extracted wiggle has the wrong sign or the wrong broadband split. Most likely the E&H normalisation leaves a residual slope in the ratio, which the 0.25-wide Gaussian then treats as signal.
status: reverted. hmcode.py is back at the committed state: terms hard-fail, CAMB clamp bounds, log-P dewiggle, nonlinear max|dev| = 1.09%
consequence_for_the_residual: the two-halo 0.56% is still unexplained. Either the dewiggle needs a correct no-wiggle split (not the naive one tried here), or the residual sits in the fdamp/k_damp normalisation after all, or the 1-halo and 2-halo descriptions each carry a small bias that partially cancels.
